$comment: Shared contract for the JIT credential the BFF broker mints and the backends verify. THREE independent implementations produce or consume this shape -- demo_api_server/services/jitCredentialBroker.js mints it, demo_api_resource_server/server.js verifies it, and demo_mcp_gateway/src/apiKeyDispatch.ts carries it. Per-service unit tests all stay green if one side renames a claim, because nothing compares them. This file is the thing they compare against: each side has a test asserting it against THIS file, so a rename fails on the side that drifted. Read by tests only -- never at runtime.
name: jit-credential
signingKey: the backend's own service key (API_RESOURCE_SERVER_API_KEY) used as an HMAC secret, so nothing new is provisioned and the static key stops travelling on the wire

claims.iss: constant 'bff-broker' -- the backend rejects any other issuer
claims.aud: backend route segment this credential is valid for, e.g. 'mortgage'. The backend gates on this because it always knows its own route from req.path and so needs no route->tool table
claims.tool: MCP tool name. Audit and trace ONLY -- the backend does not gate on it
claims.jti: unique id, for replay defence and the audit record
claims.exp: expiry (seconds). Short by design -- a leaked credential is valid for one route, for seconds

verifierMustReject.iss: a credential whose issuer is not 'bff-broker'
verifierMustReject.aud: a credential minted for a different backend route, or with no route binding at all
